description: Proves bad input is refused (an attacker thumbprint given as ours, and Remove without a thumbprint or without a relay), that Detect and Remove on a runner with no ScreenConnect report CLEAN, read both registry views and write the UDF summary, and that a second run is harmless. Then it plants an infected machine (our client, a client from another instance, and the RelayTrap folder, temp file, task and Run value, all with reserved example names) and proves Detect reports every item and deletes nothing, Remove deletes them all and saves evidence while leaving our client alone, and a Detect afterwards is clean. The planted clients are services pointing at an empty executable. Defender exclusions are skipped because GitHub's image excludes whole drives on purpose. Uninstalling a real MSI-installed client, and our own client still connecting afterwards, are Tier 2 on an internal VM.

steps.label: Unknown mode is refused
Remove without known thumbprints is refused
Remove without a known relay is refused
A published attacker thumbprint given as ours is refused
A malformed thumbprint is refused

UDF summary written where the Datto agent reads it
steps.name: Custom250

steps.label: Second Detect run is harmless
Several thumbprints, upper case, separated by a semicolon and a space, are accepted
Remove with nothing to remove changes nothing
Remove with nothing found saves no evidence

Plant an infected machine: our client, a client from another instance (relay.example.net), the RelayTrap folder, a sckit-test file in Windows\Temp, a harmless TrapWatch task and a RelayTrapLiteAlert Run value
steps.run:
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
$pf = ${env:ProgramFiles(x86)}
foreach ($c in @(@{ thumb = '0123456789abcdef'; relay = 'relay.example.com' }, @{ thumb = 'aaaabbbbccccdddd'; relay = 'relay.example.net' })) {
    $name = 'ScreenConnect Client ({0})' -f $c.thumb
    $dir  = Join-Path $pf $name
    New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $dir | Out-Null
    $exe  = Join-Path $dir 'ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe'
    Set-Content -LiteralPath $exe -Value ''
    $bin  = '"{0}" "?e=Access&y=Guest&h={1}&p=8041"' -f $exe, $c.relay
    New-Service -Name $name -BinaryPathName $bin -StartupType Manual | Out-Null
}
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path 'C:\ProgramData\RelayTrap' | Out-Null
Set-Content -LiteralPath 'C:\ProgramData\RelayTrap\payload.txt' -Value 'test payload'
New-Item -ItemType File -Force -Path 'C:\Windows\Temp\sckit-test' | Out-Null
$action  = New-ScheduledTaskAction -Execute 'cmd.exe' -Argument '/c exit 0'
$trigger = New-ScheduledTaskTrigger -Once -At (Get-Date).AddYears(1)
Register-ScheduledTask -TaskName 'TrapWatch' -Action $action -Trigger $trigger -User 'SYSTEM' -Force | Out-Null
New-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run' -Name 'RelayTrapLiteAlert' -Value 'cmd.exe /c exit 0' -Force | Out-Null
'planted'

steps.label: Detect on the planted machine reports every planted item, keeps ours, and changes nothing
outputContains: NOT OUR INSTANCE: ScreenConnect client thumb=aaaabbbbccccdddd relay=relay.example.net

steps.label: Detect left the planted payload alone
Detect left the planted temp file alone
Remove deletes the other instance's client and every planted indicator, saves evidence, and the re-check finds nothing left
Every planted item is gone, our client is untouched, the evidence log names what was removed, and a zip was saved
Detect after Remove is clean, still sees our client, and notes the saved evidence
outputContains: An earlier Remove run saved evidence

steps.label: Tier 2 (a runner has no real MSI-installed client to uninstall, and nothing to connect to): on an internal VM with our client and a second real ScreenConnect client from another instance, Remove (with our real thumbprint and relay) uninstalls the other one through msiexec and ours keeps working
Tier 2: a real workstation shows its summary in the chosen Datto UDF after the agent's next check-in
